answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it can act; a Wesolowski proof lets peers check the result cheaply. GPUs may run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shortcut the dependent squarings within any clone, so each identity still incurs a hardware-bound delay. Like a dune-carved river constrained by a canyon, progress follows a sequential path, making mass Sybil creation costly and time-limited.
